name: Winter Car Checklist
description: A checklist for preparing a car for winter weather.

items.text: Test the battery's charge and health before the cold arrives.
items.note: Cold cuts battery capacity; a marginal battery often fails in winter.

items.text: Clean corrosion from terminals and confirm they are tight.
Check the alternator is charging and belts are sound.
Confirm the battery is securely mounted with no case damage.
Carry jumper cables or a portable jump starter.
Replace a battery older than four to five years before winter.
Fit winter tires as a set of four if your climate warrants them.
Check tread depth; winter grip drops sharply on worn tires.
Set tire pressures, since cold air lowers them noticeably.
items.note: Check pressures on a cold morning and top up to the door-jamb spec.

items.text: Carry chains or traction aids where required by law or conditions.
Confirm the spare is inflated and accessible.
Verify the TPMS light is off after adjusting pressures.
Check coolant and confirm the antifreeze mix suits expected lows.
items.note: Test the freeze protection rating; weak coolant can freeze and crack the engine.

items.text: Switch to winter-grade windshield washer fluid that resists freezing.
Check engine oil; consider a winter-appropriate grade per the manual.
Verify brake and power steering fluid levels.
Inspect hoses and belts that stiffen and crack in the cold.
Top up and test the heater and defroster operation.
Replace worn wipers or fit winter blades that shed ice.
Test all lights — they matter more in short winter days.
Keep an ice scraper and snow brush in the car.
Check door and window seals to prevent freezing shut.
Apply a lock de-icer or treat seals against freezing.
Keep headlights and indicators clear of snow and salt grime.
Pack a warm blanket, gloves, hat and spare warm clothing.
Carry a small shovel and sand, salt or traction mats.
Stock a flashlight, warning triangle and reflective vest.
Bring water, non-perishable snacks and any medications.
Pack a first-aid kit and hand warmers.
Keep a phone charger and power bank fully charged.
Keep the fuel tank at least half full to reduce condensation and ensure heat.
Clear all snow and ice from the roof, windows and lights before driving.
Confirm roadside assistance and insurance are current.
Practice gentle braking and longer following distances on ice.
Check weather and road conditions before each trip.
Tell someone your route and expected arrival in severe weather.

faq.q: What is a winter car checklist?
faq.a: It's a seasonal prep guide that readies a car for cold weather — battery, tires, antifreeze, visibility and an emergency kit — so drivers can start, stop and drive safely through snow, ice and freezing temperatures.

faq.q: When should I winterize my car?
faq.a: Complete winter prep before the first hard freeze, ideally in late fall, so there is time to fit winter tires, replace a weak battery and adjust fluids before cold weather sets in.

In regions with sustained snow, ice or temperatures near or below freezing, winter tires give far better grip and braking than all-season tires. Check local laws, your manual and conditions, and fit them as a set of four.

faq.q: What should be in a winter emergency kit?
faq.a: Carry a blanket, warm clothing, gloves, an ice scraper, a small shovel, traction aids like sand or mats, a flashlight, jumper cables, water, snacks, and a fully charged phone with a power bank.

faq.q: Is this available as a printable PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Print the winter car checklist to work through in the garage, or download the PDF to complete on your phone before the cold sets in.
